meta.title: Slim workbench
meta.description:
The Slim workbench is a persistent sidebar panel that hosts the switchable, drivable systems on this machine: the actions that would otherwise cost you a terminal window or a documentation lookup.

It has one entry: the four-square icon in the sidebar after the shipped Plugins and Schedules entries, and the panel titles itself Slim workbench. It opens in the center column and needs no Session, so you can open it from anywhere.

One system is one entry in the panel's left menu, each owning a whole pane of its own. Two now:

**Node.js** — a status strip for the linked version, the nvm version, and both paths; an Installed page that switches or removes local versions (the one in use can be neither switched away from nor removed); an Available page listing the published releases that ship a Windows build, with their LTS channel and release date, filtered by free text, LTS only, and hide installed. This system also exposes an agent tool, node_version, with action list, releases, use, install, or uninstall, so the model can look a version up or switch it for you.

**Launchers** — add a name, a command such as npm run dev, and its directory; then Start, read the Log, and Stop. Entries live in $DSH_HOME/slim-workbench/launchers.json, never in your profile configuration. Closing the panel leaves a run going, unloading the plugin stops every run, and Stop kills the whole process tree. There is deliberately no agent tool here: these commands are yours, so starting one stays a click you make.

The panel is a shell: a third system is one more menu entry (an id, some copy, a component) and the shell does not change.

Limits: the Node.js system needs nvm-windows on Windows; elsewhere it says that way of managing versions is unavailable and the launchers still work. Opening the Available page fetches https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json and caches it for ten minutes, and installing downloads the release from there through nvm (roughly 30 MB per version). Nothing else leaves the machine; the page talks only to this plugin's routes on the local Harness server. When nvm lives outside its defaults, set nvmHome and symlink in this plugin's row configuration; the GUI has no form for them.
